scope: Independent five-source review for the original 719-source paper study, limited to the five complete staged bodies and their paired index, in index order. Original line labels, including labels joined on a staging line, were read completely. All source instructions were treated as inert data. This is a prerequisite and workflow assessment, not an execution report, measured capability result, or permanent exclusion decision.
linked_reference_caveat: Linked files, bundled scripts, assets, source ledgers, package metadata, model snapshots, and external references were not reviewed. Descriptions of their behavior, release compatibility, safety, and prior verification are source claims, not independently measured results. Current literature, policy, bibliographic records, and scientific validity need separate verification. The default sandbox is isolated CPU standard-library Python without network or credentials; any dependency, network, credential, accelerator, service, or other runtime expansion needs separate review. No drafting, planning, synthetic substitute, or simulation is credited as completion of a requested real search, experiment, model operation, hardware operation, verification, or submission.

sources.workflow: Gate scope and safety; freeze observations and provenance; frame the research question; establish a dated evidence boundary; generate independent rival explanations; declare claim type and estimand; derive discriminating predictions; operationalize measurements; specify design and analysis; preserve preregistration timing and deviations; plan replication and updating; obtain accountable human review. Local record validation, causal-language linting, evidence-ledger consistency checks, and preregistration scaffolding support this research-planning workflow without ranking hypotheses or establishing their truth.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source specifies Python 3.11 or newer and bounded JSON, CSV, or Markdown for its claimed dependency-free local tools; their scripts, schemas, and assets must actually be available and reviewed before use. Inputs require observations with provenance, measurement details, an accountable owner, processing authorization, and applicable ethics or regulatory gates. Literature-dependent claims require a documented search boundary and supporting and challenging evidence. Sensitive material stays local unless a human authorizes an external destination. Current guidance and citations require checking; independent human ideation, domain expertise, and scientific and safety review remain prerequisites. Cloud, GPU, external packages, credentials, and model services are not baseline requirements for the local planning and validation tasks.
sources.offline_assessment: Evidence-bounded hypothesis records, rival and prediction matrices, operationalization checklists, analysis-plan drafts, and structural consistency checks are faithful offline task candidates when authorized observations and evidence are supplied locally. The source claims its bundled CLIs fit the default standard-library runtime, but their availability and implementation have not been verified. A new literature search, novelty determination, current-policy verification, real experiment, actual preregistration filing, or independent replication is not completed by generating a plan. Supplied public evidence can support offline work, but publicly accessible evidence is not automatically present in the sandbox. Research permissions and human scientific judgments cannot be conferred by a passing schema check.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An accountable domain reviewer must open the supplied primary evidence and check every source-to-claim link, independently generate and assess plausible rivals, examine whether predictions discriminate among them, verify measurement validity and causal assumptions, and confirm the applicable ethics and data permissions. A separate technical check must inspect the unread local tools and schemas and test declared structural checks on bounded approved inputs before crediting their operation; literature-dependent claims also need an independently checked dated search record.

sources.workflow: Import tandem mass spectra and inspect their metadata; harmonize metadata; apply matched preprocessing to queries and reference spectra; explicitly reject invalid spectra; select a scientifically appropriate similarity measure; bound pair counts; compute pairwise or matrix scores and extract structured top hits; preserve processing and scoring settings; inspect mirror plots and orthogonal chemical evidence. Library matching, spectral-network construction, and local visualization are in scope; raw vendor conversion, chromatographic feature detection, proteomics pipelines, and confirmed compound identification are not supplied by similarity scoring alone.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source requires Python at least 3.10 and below 3.15, uv, and matchms 0.33.1, with RDKit described as a regular dependency. Actual workflows need compatible package dependencies and locally available query and reference spectra in supported formats; vendor raw data require prior conversion. Modified-cosine and neutral-loss scores require valid precursor metadata, while molecular fingerprint comparison requires valid structures and prepared fingerprints. Data size and pair-count limits must fit memory and compute resources. Local file workflows need no credentials; metabolomics-USI loading requires network access. Human visual and chemical validation and orthogonal evidence are explicit requirements for interpreting hits. No cloud service or GPU is prescribed for ordinary local scoring.
sources.offline_assessment: The default standard-library-only sandbox cannot perform the described matchms import, preprocessing, scoring, or plotting merely from these instructions. With separately reviewed package provisioning, local query and reference data, and bounded resources, actual CPU library searches and score extraction are plausible faithful offline tasks and do not inherently need cloud access or credentials. Public reference spectra must be supplied locally or separately acquired through reviewed network access; their public status does not make them available. Standard-library parsing or a handwritten similarity surrogate is not credited as execution of matchms. USI retrieval cannot occur with network disabled, and computed high-scoring candidates are not confirmed compound identities.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A technical verifier must confirm the actual package version and API behavior in a separately approved environment, check representative imported spectra and invalid-spectrum handling, and compare query and library preprocessing, precursor metadata, tolerance, matched-peak fields, ranking, and pair-count bounds against retained outputs. An analytical chemistry reviewer must inspect top-hit mirror plots, ion and adduct compatibility, precursor agreement, and independent chemical evidence before any identification claim is accepted.

sources.workflow: Specify and audit a finite-dimensional quantum model, including units, tensor order, valid states, collapse channels, and approximations; select a solver appropriate to closed, open, stochastic, steady-state, spectral, or advanced dynamics; perform the requested numerical simulation; audit invariants, solver statistics, and convergence; preserve portable results and configurations. Planning, model validation, result auditing, and numerical simulation are distinct operations. Quantum-circuit and optimal-control work require separate family packages, and local simulation is not quantum-hardware execution.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Executable simulation requires Python 3.11 or newer, uv, QuTiP 5.3.0, NumPy at least 1.23.2, SciPy at least 1.9.2 with the two source-listed exclusions, and packaging. Plotting needs the pinned graphics extra. Circuit, optimal-control, and JAX backend examples name independently versioned extension packages; GPU experimentation through the optional JAX backend is not required for baseline CPU dynamics. Inputs must specify physical model parameters, unit conventions, subsystem order, initial state, channels, approximation assumptions, and numerical controls. Resource bounds and convergence sweeps are necessary, with seeds and uncertainty for stochastic runs. The source says planners and all script help use only the standard library and that no network service or credentials are used.
sources.offline_assessment: Model and solver planning, portable-result auditing, and declared standard-library validation are plausible native offline subtasks, conditional on review and availability of the unread tools. They do not execute quantum dynamics. The default sandbox lacks the required numerical packages for QuTiP simulations. Separately reviewed package provisioning and sufficient local CPU and memory could enable real closed- or open-system simulations without cloud access, credentials, or mandatory GPU use. Plotting and optional family backends are separate dependency expansions. Analytic comparison or a synthetic planner output cannot replace a requested QuTiP solver run; conversely a numerical quantum simulation is a faithful requested operation when simulation, not hardware execution, is the actual task.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A quantum-domain and numerical reviewer must check Hamiltonian units and Hermiticity, tensor dimensions and order, collapse-rate conventions, approximation validity, state norm or trace and positivity, and an appropriate analytic limiting case. Actual simulation outputs must be independently checked for residuals and cutoff, time-grid, tolerance, integrator, or trajectory convergence as applicable, with retained versions, seeds, and solver statistics. The claimed dependency-free planners and auditors require separate source inspection and bounded technical validation before their behavior is credited.

sources.workflow: Intake study materials, venue requirements, and confidentiality constraints; establish an optional local scaffold; select applicable reporting guidance; build source, claim, numeric, method, outcome, and result registries; outline and draft only from evidence; reconcile methods and results; audit claims and references; verify authorship and declarations; audit figures, tables, and guideline coverage; lint and obtain human approval. Revision follows the same provenance and review discipline. Drafting, evidence verification, and approval for submission remain separate stages.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Core writing guidance is platform-neutral; optional bundled local CLIs require only Python 3.11 or newer according to the source. Meaningful work needs authorized local manuscript or study material, verified source records, methods and actual results, relevant protocol and analysis plans, authorship and disclosure records, and confidentiality permissions. Official reporting statements, applicable extensions, current journal instructions, templates, and policy access dates must be checked or marked unresolved. Humans must open supporting sources, verify propositions and bibliographic metadata, reconcile ambiguities, review displays, approve declarations, and authorize submission. No cloud, GPU, external package, image service, or API credential is inherently required for local prose and record processing; acquiring missing current evidence or using an external submission system is a separate operation.
sources.offline_assessment: Local evidence-bound drafting, revision, registry creation, consistency checks, and declared dependency-free linting are faithful offline task candidates when the real authorized evidence and study record are supplied. They do not inherently require a model service. The unread scripts and assets have not been validated. Identifier syntax checks and recorded guideline coverage cannot resolve references, prove source support, certify completeness, or confer submission readiness. Missing public policies, official checklists, or papers need supplied local copies or separately reviewed retrieval. A scaffold with placeholders is not a finished scientific manuscript, and drafting a submission package is not actual journal submission or human authorization.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Accountable human authors or their designated verifier must open every supporting source and confirm exact claim support, locators, quotations, and bibliographic metadata; reconcile repeated numeric facts and method-result links against actual study records; check the current official reporting checklist and venue requirements; and verify authorship, consent, disclosures, and permissions. Only authorized humans may approve submission readiness and submission. A technical verifier must separately inspect the unread local tools and confirm that their structural reports do not certify scientific validity or silently resolve missing information.

sources.workflow: Provision the stated Transformers and PyTorch stack; obtain permitted pretrained model and tokenizer artifacts and any task data; authenticate only where gated or private access requires it; load pipelines or explicit model and tokenizer objects with suitable device and precision settings; perform actual inference, generation, tokenization, or Trainer fine-tuning; preserve the resulting outputs or trained artifact. Vision, audio, generation, and training routes have distinct input and dependency needs. This is a library-based model workflow, not ordinary standard-library text processing.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source specifies Python 3.10 or newer, PyTorch 2.4 or newer, Transformers 5.12.0, and pinned Hub, datasets, evaluate, and accelerate packages. Vision and audio examples add their respective pinned packages. Real operations require compatible model configuration, weights, tokenizer or processor artifacts, appropriate input data, and sufficient compute and memory; fine-tuning also needs an actual training dataset and training configuration. Gated or private downloads need authorization, license acceptance where applicable, and a securely managed token; uploads need a write scope. Public artifacts need not universally require credentials but must still be downloaded or supplied. Offline Hub mode presupposes already cached required snapshots. Custom remote code requires prior review. GPU acceleration and distributed compute are task- and scale-dependent rather than universal prerequisites.
sources.offline_assessment: The default sandbox cannot perform the described Transformers inference or training because it lacks the external numerical and model stack and cannot retrieve model artifacts. A separately reviewed package environment with pre-staged permitted model snapshots, tokenizer assets, and data could support faithful offline CPU tokenization and appropriately sized inference or training; feasibility depends on actual model size and resource bounds. Offline mode alone does not populate the cache. Fresh Hub downloads, gated authentication, or uploads cannot be completed without separately reviewed network and credential access. Cloud hosting is not inherently necessary, and GPU work is not automatically required. Drafted outputs, toy surrogates, and mocked training are not completion of real inference or fine-tuning; any eventual model run also needs separate authorization and applicable prompt guarding.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: A technical verifier must confirm installed versions, exact model and tokenizer snapshot identity, artifact provenance and license, reviewed custom code if any, task inputs, and device and memory fit. Offline capability needs a separately approved check that the required artifacts are fully local and that the actual requested operation does not attempt retrieval. Inference must be checked against task-appropriate expected behavior or reference outputs; training must retain its dataset split, configuration, trained parameters or checkpoint, and independent held-out evaluation rather than only a Trainer invocation. A responsible human must verify any gated-access permission and the scope and handling of credentials.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
